key_insight: For sim-to-real material estimation from drop videos, consistently measured 2D motion transfers better than explicit 3D tracklets, despite the opposite ranking in simulation.
engineering_relevance: A single drop video can estimate density-normalized stiffness and, when plastic deformation occurs, yield stress, enabling video-based characterization of deformable objects.
method: Train a feed-forward predictor, PhysReader, entirely in simulation.
Combine video with short 2D optical-flow tracklets.
Learn a 3D lift by matching a teacher with access to exact 3D deformation.
evidence_signal: On PhysReader-Real—16 everyday objects dropped five times each, with jointly fitted references checked against tensile tests—PhysReader outperformed other inputs and baselines except a prediction-initialized optimizer taking 49 minutes per video versus 12 seconds.
watch_item: Validation covers only 16 objects, and synthetic accuracy alone can misrank inputs for real-world transfer.
paper_title: What a Drop Reveals: Sim-to-Real Material Estimation for Deformable Objects from Video
